input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate: Talk to her directly and calmly. Acknowledge that the earlier conversation may have created expectations, explain that you need to check the facts before making any promise, and set a short follow-up. Keep the financing process separate and avoid arguing over memory in the first conversation.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Do two separate things, in this order. First, have a humane conversation that names the concern without conceding the equity claim: you will review written notes, emails, and board-approved terms before making any cap-table commitment. Second, protect the financing deadline by telling investors only what is true now: no new grant or correction exists until evidence and board process support it. If she has written evidence, inspect it quickly; if she only has a memory of an informal promise, offer a bounded review path rather than a negotiation under pressure.

step6_output.answer_core: Start with a short, calm check‑in. Acknowledge that the earlier conversation may have created expectations, but make clear you’re not confirming any equity change until you review written notes, emails, and prior approvals. Set a concrete follow‑up window, such as within 48–72 hours. Keep the financing process separate: investors should hear only what is currently true — no new grant or correction exists unless and until the evidence and board process support it. If she brings written evidence, review it quickly. If she has only a recollection, outline a bounded review path rather than negotiating under deadline pressure.
